summary: Add observability to an Effect server: traces, logs and metrics exported to an OpenTelemetry collector, with trace ids in the server logs.
description: Add OpenTelemetry to the Effect server in an API, Astro or React Router project. One observability layer exports traces, logs and metrics over OTLP when an endpoint is configured and does nothing otherwise, so development and tests need no collector. Each request gets one server span named by its route, log records carry trace ids, and defect messages stay out of exported data. Tests use an in-memory tracer and a loopback receiver. Browser code is not instrumented, and choosing and running a telemetry backend is left to the project.
seoDescription: OpenTelemetry traces, logs and metrics over OTLP for Effect servers, with trace ids in logs and tests that need no collector.

projectExamples.title: Traced order API
projectExamples.description: An illustrative JSON API whose request spans show which service call made a slow request, exported to a local collector during development.

projectExamples.title: Server-rendered app with correlated logs
projectExamples.description: An illustrative React Router app whose loader and action logs carry trace ids, so one slow page load can be followed across log lines and spans.

plain.whatItIs: Sends the server's timing records, logs and counts to a monitoring tool you choose, so slow requests can be traced.
goodAt: Finding which step inside a request was slow, such as a call to another service
Matching each server log line to the request it came from
Running tests without a monitoring tool or any account
notGoodAt: Browser screens; it only watches the server, so use a browser monitoring tool there.
